verdict.rationale: The evidence shows Highnote offers collaborative authorization for real-time approve/decline decisions, and spend rules that can key off MCC. However, nothing documents the contents of an authorization event payload: merchant name, MCC, enhanced merchant data, wallet or entry-mode details, and partial-approval or incremental-auth signals are all unevidenced. MCC-based spend rules are a related control, not proof that authorization events carry this context.

support.subject: As a developer, every authorization event carries decision-grade context — merchant name and MCC, enhanced merchant data, wallet and entry-mode details, partial-approval and incremental-auth signals
